data.title: Harry makes first public appearance since return to UK
data.description: LONDON - Prince Harry on Thursday made his first public appearance since his shock return to Britain from the United States with his family three weeks ago.

data.title: Oversight Board blasts 'inadequate' Meta safeguards for AI deepfakes
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Meta on Thursday moved to remove AI-generated videos targeting two women, including a British politician, after the tech giant's Oversight Board blasted its "fundamentally inadequate" safeguards against proliferating deepfakes.

data.title: Russians begin voting in controlled election as war drags
data.description: MOSCOW - Polling stations opened early Friday in Russia's Far East, kicking off a three-day election that President Vladimir Putin's party is all but guaranteed to win in the fifth year of war with Ukraine.

data.title: Third malaria death in Germany from outbreak tied to Frankfurt airport
data.description: FRANKFURT (GERMANY) - One person died from malaria in Frankfurt and another was infected, local health officials said Thursday, the latest cases from a malaria outbreak linked to the city's airport.

data.title: French fishermen block ports over petrol prices
data.description: NICE (FRANCE) - Fishermen on Thursday blocked the entrance to two ports and a petrol depot in southern France in protest at rising fuel prices linked to the US-Iran war.

data.title: Macron hosts Lebanon security talks as UN mission nears end
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The leaders of France, Lebanon and Jordan have met in Paris to discuss international support for the cash-strapped Lebanese army and the creation of a new force to succeed a longstanding UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon.

data.title: Sweden's left-wing wins election thriller
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Sweden's left-wing opposition won a narrow majority in the country's general election after the vote count ended Thursday, but faces laborious negotiations to form a government.

data.title: King Charles disputes claims in book by Princess Diana's brother
data.description: LONDON - Britain's King Charles III has taken the rare step of hitting back at criticism after Princess Diana's brother alleged that the monarch acted insensitively following her death in a car crash three decades ago.

data.title: Ireland to boycott Eurovision 2027 over Gaza
data.description: DUBLIN - Ireland has decided not to participate in or broadcast next year's Eurovision Song Contest, public broadcaster RTE said Thursday, citing the "ongoing loss of lives in Gaza".

data.title: Ninth woman found dead in South Africa killing spree
data.description: JOHANNESBURG — South African police on Thursday recovered the body of a ninth woman east of Johannesburg in two months, as a string of murders continues to stoke public anxiety.

data.title: Palestinians turn rugged caves into homes
data.description: YATTA, Palestinian Territories - Palestinian herder Mohammed Emar has set up a fully functional home for his family where his daughters can even sing karaoke. Only it is inside a cave after the Israeli army demolished his two houses.

data.title: ‘One of the kindest people’ facing execution in Iran
data.description: On the nights of January 8 and 9, twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi joined thousands of others in protests against the Iranian authorities in the central city of Isfahan.

data.title: King Charles to call for ‘reassurances’ over AI
data.description: CUMNOCK, Scotland - King Charles III will urge tech giants to ensure that artificial intelligence is geared to serve humanity and that mankind does “not lose control”, during a conference in Scotland on Thursday.

data.title: Lebanon security talks focus on replacing UN mission
data.description: PARIS - The leaders of France, Lebanon and Jordan on Thursday met in Paris to discuss international support for the cash-strapped Lebanese army and the creation of a new force to succeed a longstanding UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon.

data.title: Ukraine plans record defence spending in 2027
data.description: KYIV - The Ukrainian government plans to spend a record two thirds of its budget on defence next year as costs mount in its war with Russia, government documents showed.

data.title: EU defends Canada alliance plan after Trump threat
data.description: BRUSSELS - EU chief Ursula von der Leyen’s proposal to make Canada an “associate member” of the bloc is not aimed against the United States, the European Commission said Thursday after President Donald Trump threatened trade ties over the plan.

data.title: Leader’s sister says only ‘idiots’ think North Korea will give up nukes
data.description: SEOUL - The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said Thursday that the country’s nuclear-armed status was “absolute”, calling those hoping for its denuclearisation “idiots”.

data.title: NASA discovers new, ’once in a century’ Moon crater
data.description: WASHINGTON - A researcher at NASA has found a massive, recently-formed crater on the Moon, a rare occurrence that only happens “once in a century or even longer”, according to scientists.

data.title: Australia to cut migration to fix housing crisis
data.description: SYDNEY - Australia will reduce migration by curbing "visa hopping", tightening rules on students and working holiday makers as well as cracking down on overstayers, its interior minister said Thursday, as the far-right surges in the polls.

data.title: Global river flows lowest in decades, UN says
data.description: GENEVA - Rivers worldwide experienced one of their driest years in decades in 2025, according to the ​World Meteorological ⁠Organization, reflecting declining water storage across the Earth’s surface and raising concerns about future supplies.

data.title: Cash-for-photos scheme turns Indonesian poachers into protectors
data.description: KAPUAS HULU, Indonesia - Villager Octavius wades through the forest in rubber boots and tattered joggers, ears pricked, eyes peeled, a telephoto lens on his phone primed to capture orangutans, monkeys or birds.

data.title: Taylor Swift’s husband among Ponzi scheme victims
data.description: WASHINGTON - Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, the husband of singer Taylor Swift, was among investors defrauded out of millions of dollars by a financial adviser who is going to prison.

data.title: Lula to tell Trump to ‘stay out’ of Brazil’s elections
data.description: BRASILIA - President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Wednesday he will tell US President Donald Trump “not to meddle in Brazil’s elections” next week during the United Nations General Assembly.

data.title: US denies Palestinian leader Abbas visa to attend UN
data.description: WASHINGTON - The United States has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, a source familiar with the case said Wednesday.

data.title: India's transgender amendment leaves many in limbo
data.description: HYDERABAD (INDIA) - When transgender woman Kali Sidharth Medepalli began hormone replacement therapy in India, she expected to complete her medical transition and undergo surgery within a year.

data.title: US Fed raises rates to tackle 'too high' inflation, irking Trump
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, defying President Donald Trump's demand for cuts, as central bank chief Kevin Warsh stressed the need to combat inflation that has been "too high" for "too long."

data.title: NFL Chiefs' Kelce among investors bilked in Ponzi scheme
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, husband of singer Taylor Swift, was among investors defrauded out of millions of dollars by a financial adviser who is going to prison.

data.title: Trump to host Xi amid pomp, low expectations
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US military honor guard has been rehearsing and the new White House helipad is ready. But will Xi Jinping and Donald Trump achieve lift-off at their summit next week?

data.title: HK touts itself as gateway to riches
data.description: HONG KONG: Hong Kong is positioning itself as a "Superconnector" and "Super Valuator" under China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), promoting the city as a gateway linking Chinese companies with overseas markets and international investors with China and Asia.

data.title: Candidate for UN chief calls for AI regulation akin to nuclear weapons
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - A contender to lead the UN called Wednesday for artificial intelligence to be regulated like nuclear weapons, warning that a Third World War would be fought with the emerging technology.

data.title: French ex-minister Dati goes on trial in Renault-Nissan corruption case
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France's ex-culture minister Rachida Dati appeared in court Wednesday on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan group, just months after her bruising defeat in the Paris mayoral race.

data.title: Gaza apartment block collapse leaves 21 dead
data.description: GAZA CITY (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Gaza authorities said Wednesday that 21 people including five children had died after an apartment building collapsed from damage sustained in earlier Israeli strikes.

data.title: 'We're losing control,' AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio tells AFP
data.description: MONTREAL (CANADA) - The Canadian computer scientist considered one of the founders of AI, Yoshua Bengio, told AFP that humanity is "losing control" of the technology and that the world needs guardrails similar to nuclear arms controls.

data.title: Fuel prices stirring unrest around the world
data.description: Social unrest and political squabbles have broken out around the world over soaring energy costs, with protests erupting in the Americas, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

data.title: Malaysia seeks talks with Myanmar president on Rohingya
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Wednesday he would invite Myanmar’s junta chief-turned-President Min Aung Hlaing for an official visit in return for his government accepting the return of thousands of Rohingya Muslim refugees.
